info.title: How much should you eat for balanced nutrition?
body: Adults need on average 1,800–2,400 kcal/day depending on sex, age and activity level (roughly 1,800–2,200 kcal for women, 2,200–2,800 kcal for men).
A balanced meal should cover 4 groups: carbs (rice/noodles/potatoes), protein (meat/fish/eggs/beans), vegetables, and healthy fats.
Aim for 3 regular meals at consistent times — try not to skip breakfast or eat too late at night.
This is general reference information, not a substitute for personal nutrition advice from a doctor or dietitian.

info.title: When is the best time to exercise?
body: WHO recommends adults get at least 150 minutes/week of moderate activity (or 75 minutes of vigorous activity).
Early morning (1-2 hours after waking) helps you stay alert all day; late afternoon (4-7 PM) is when body temperature and muscle strength peak — good for heavier training.
Avoid training close to bedtime (within 1-2 hours) as it can make it harder to fall asleep.
Aim for at least 1-2 rest days per week so your body can recover.

water.subtitle: Cast your vote below. Each device can vote once per day.

info.title: How much water is enough?
body: Adults: women about 2 liters/day (~8 cups of 250ml), men about 2.5–3 liters/day.
Children 4–8 years old: about 1.2 liters/day; teens 9–18: about 1.6–1.9 liters/day.
Spread it out — 150–250ml per serving, roughly every 1-2 hours. Don't wait until you're thirsty.
Drink more during intense exercise or hot weather. General reference only, individual needs vary.

info.title: How much sleep is enough?
body: Adults (18-64): 7-9 hours/night. Older adults (65+): 7-8 hours. Teens: 8-10 hours.
Try to go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day, weekends included.
Avoid phone/computer screens for at least 30-60 minutes before bed.
Keep your bedroom dark, quiet and cool (around 25-27°C / 77-80°F) to fall asleep more easily.
